# Labelens (food-scanner): handoff notes for Copilot

Copilot in VS Code loads this file automatically. User-facing docs are in `README.md`; the build plan is
`tasks/plan.md` and progress is `tasks/todo.md`. Last updated: 2026-10-26.

## What this is

Labelens answers "can I eat this?" for travellers. The user sets what they avoid (pork, halal, vegetarian, vegan,
the 14 standard allergens, or custom words), then scans a barcode, photographs a food, or searches by name. A plain
verdict goes at the top (e.g. **CONTAINS PORK**), with the evidence and the matching words highlighted in the
ingredient list. Caffeine and nutrition are shown below it.

## Safety rules (the core of the product; never weaken them)

- **Never say "safe".** Verdicts: **Contains**, **May contain**, **Can't tell**, **Not found in the listed
  ingredients** (explicitly not a guarantee).
- Missing or thin data is never good news: no ingredient list, a very short or unfinished list, or a declared
  allergen the list doesn't explain → **Can't tell**.
- Labels like "halal" or "vegan" only add a note; they never lower a finding.
- A failed lookup is never shown as "not found": say the lookup failed and list words to check on the package.
- Photo and name-search results are typical USDA recipes, not labelled products: at most **May contain**,
  otherwise **Can't tell**.
- The original ingredient text always stays visible, even with a translation.
- Word-boundary traps are tested: "porcini" is not pork, "peanut" vs "nut". Hidden sources (gelatin, E441, E120,
  rennet, "natural flavours") are **May contain** or **Can't tell**, never ignored.

## Stack and commands

- **Next.js 16.4.3** (App Router), React 19.3, TypeScript 5, ESLint 9, Vitest 4. This Next version has breaking
  changes from older docs: read `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before using unfamiliar APIs. `AGENTS.md` is
  regenerated by `next dev`; leave it alone.
- On-device photo recognition: MobileCLIP via `@huggingface/transformers` (~43 MB, downloaded once in the browser).
  Barcodes: native `BarcodeDetector` or the `barcode-detector` (ZXing WASM) fallback.
- Data: Open Food Facts + USDA FoodData Central (barcode), bundled USDA FNDDS generic foods
  (`data/generic-foods.json`, ~5,400 foods). No paid APIs or keys; `USDA_API_KEY` is optional (`.env.example`).

```
npm run dev       # http://localhost:3000 (camera works only on localhost or HTTPS)
npm test          # vitest: 96 tests including real-product fixtures (all passing on 2026-10-26)
npm run lint
npm run build
npm run embeddings    # after editing data/foods.ts (a test fails if embeddings drift)
npm run usda -- path/to/surveyDownload.json   # refresh generic foods from an FNDDS release
```

## Layout

| Path | Job |
|---|---|
| `lib/diet.ts` | what each diet/allergen matches: OFF taxonomy tags, multilingual word regexes, E-numbers (pure) |
| `lib/verdict.ts` | product + profile → findings; decides when data is too thin to trust (pure) |
| `lib/report.ts` | Open Food Facts / USDA records → a report |
| `lib/lookup.ts`, `lib/profile.ts`, `lib/translate.ts` | failure states, saved choices (localStorage, migrates the old `labelens-my-allergens` key), translation links |
| `lib/recognize.ts`, `data/foods.ts` | on-device photo recognition and the ~155 foods it knows |
| `lib/generic.ts` | search over the bundled USDA generic foods |
| `app/api/food-scanner/route.ts` | barcode lookup; `app/api/search` (name search) and `app/api/identify` (photo nutrition) |
| `components/` | `FoodScanner`, `VerdictBanner`, `ProfileSetup`, `SavedLibrary`, `LookupProblem` |

Privacy: the user's choices stay in the browser; photos never leave the device (only the recognized food's name is
sent); only the barcode goes to the server.

## Status

- All 8 planned tasks are done, and photo recognition, name search and the saved library were merged into `main`.
- **Not done (human checkpoints):** A: scan 5 real products and compare against their physical labels.
  B: try it on a phone over HTTPS before sharing it.
- Git: `main` tracks `https://github.com/elie-gbn/food-scanner` (Elie's GitHub). The `local/photo-search-saved`
  branch is already merged into `main`.
- Known limit: the rate limiter is in-memory per server instance, so it doesn't hold on serverless. Not a safety issue.

## Working conventions

- Pure logic in `lib/` with tests next to it (`*.test.ts`). Any verdict or matching change needs a test, and real
  products go in `lib/fixtures`.
- Most files use CRLF line endings (Windows/OneDrive). Keep each file's existing endings.
- Run `npm test`, `npm run lint` and `npm run build` before calling something done.
